story_type: rocket launch seen from a camera on the rocket
hook: A camera on this rocket watched its booster tumble away over Earth.
narration: A camera bolted to this rocket watched a spent booster tumble away over Earth.
The Atlas V was carrying Boeing's Starliner capsule, with no crew aboard, on May nineteenth, 2022.
At liftoff, the camera looked straight down at the flame and the launch pad falling away.
Solid rocket boosters cannot be throttled or shut off. Once lit, they burn until the fuel is gone.
After they burned out, the rocket weighed just half of what it did at launch.
Less than three minutes in, it was fifty-six kilometers up, and the curve of the Earth filled the frame.
[short pause] Then the empty boosters let go and fell back toward the ocean.
outcome: Starliner reached the space station and landed on its airbags in the New Mexico desert six days later.

location_card.place: Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida

title: Rocket cam sees its booster fall away
description:
A camera on a United Launch Alliance Atlas V watched the launch pad fall away and the rocket's solid boosters drop off above Earth as Boeing's uncrewed Starliner OFT-2 lifted off from Cape Canaveral on May 19, 2022.

Footage: NASA KSC video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/KSC-20220519-MH-AJN01-0001-Boeing_OFT_2_Isolated_Launch_Views_1080p_3302909

facts.claim: Atlas V with Starliner launched from SLC-41, 6:54 p.m. May 19, 2022, uncrewed OFT-2
facts.source_quote: A United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket with Boeing’s CST-100 Starliner spacecraft launches from Space Launch Complex-41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, 6:54 p.m. EDT May 19, 2022. The uncrewed OFT-2 is Starliner’s second flight for NASA’s Commercial Crew Program.

extra_sources.excerpt: Boeing’s CST-100 Starliner spacecraft lands at White Sands Missile Range’s Space Harbor, Wednesday, May 25, 2022, in New Mexico. ... NASA and Boeing safely landed the company’s CST-100 Starliner spacecraft Wednesday in the desert of the western United States, completing the uncrewed Orbital Flight Test-2 (OFT-2) to the International Space Station to help prove the system is ready to fly astronauts. About four hours after departing the space station, Starliner touched down onto its airbags at 4:49 p.m. MDT, wrapping up the six-day flight, which tested the end-to-end capabilities of the crew-capable spacecraft.
